text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- A debate has started within junior coalition partner the conservative People's Party over a successor for its leader Wolfgang Schuessel, former conservative general secretary Michel Graff told Profil magazine.
- Heavy rain triggers rash of floods and mudslides across Austria.
- A price battle in Austria's do-it-yourself sector is becoming more bitter with the expansion drive of Germany's Obi chain.
- Banque Generale du Luxembourg in January started proceedings to sue Creditanstalt for over 287 million schillings, Profil magazine said.

- Coalition partner the Social Democrats would certainly not support a vote of no confidence in Foreign Minister and People's Party leader Schuessel, under fire for his alleged insulting remarks abroad, a top Social Democrat said.
- Austria will suffer a three billion schilling hole if road pricing on Austria's motorways is not introduced, a traffic expert at the workers' chamber said.
- Traders see the ATX index, which has risen 16 percent already this year, scaling further heights as it is still seen as a laggard compared to other Eurobourses.

- Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend confirms his support for Austria joining the Western military alliance NATO. Government must first make a decision and to immediately ask the people would be "the wrong way." Fasslabend also threw his support behind beleaguered Schuessel.
- The Social Democrats support a referendum on NATO membership but are against a referendum on the euro.
